settings.question: How much does flat tire repair cost in Calgary?
settings.answer: Flat tire repair costs $50 per tire at Prince Tires — one flat price, no shop fee. That covers the full job: we dismount the tire, find the puncture, clean and patch it from the inside, then remount the wheel and reset your TPMS. We rebalance the wheel if it needs it, not as a matter of course. The repair is warrantied for the life of the tire and takes about 20-30 minutes. You'll see the price confirmed when you book online.

settings.question: Can my tire be repaired, or does it need replacing?
settings.answer: It depends where the damage is. A puncture in the tread area — the part that touches the road — is usually repairable if the hole is small (roughly the size of a nail or screw) and you didn't drive far on it flat. Damage in the sidewall, a gash, or a tire that's been run flat can't be safely patched. Bring it in and we'll give you an honest look — we won't sell you a tire you don't need.

settings.question: Patch vs plug — which is the proper repair?
settings.answer: The patch. A plug is pushed into the puncture from the outside without taking the tire off — a temporary, get-home-only fix, not a real repair, and we don't do them. A proper internal patch means we dismount the tire and seal the puncture from the inside, permanently. That's the only method tire manufacturers count as a true repair, and it's what every $50 flat repair at Prince Tires uses, warrantied for the life of the tire. If you plugged a tire yourself to get off the road, bring it in and we'll patch it properly.

settings.question: How long does a flat tire repair take?
settings.answer: About 20-30 minutes. Book a time slot online and there's no waiting around — drop the vehicle, we patch the tire from the inside, rebalance the wheel if it needs it, and you're back on the road. Same-day service is usually available.

settings.question: Can you repair a puncture in the sidewall?
settings.answer: No — and no reputable shop will. The sidewall flexes constantly as you drive, so a patch there won't hold and the tire can fail at speed. Sidewall damage, including the bulges that show up after hitting a deep Calgary pothole, means the tire needs replacing. We'll show you the damage and explain exactly why.

settings.question: My tire keeps losing air slowly — can you find the leak?
settings.answer: Yes. Slow leaks are one of the most common things we see, especially through a Calgary winter. The cause could be a small puncture, a corroded rim, a tired valve stem, or just the cold — tire pressure drops about 1-2 PSI for every 5°C the temperature falls. We dunk the tire, pinpoint exactly where the air is escaping, and fix the real cause instead of just topping you up.

settings.heading: Flat Tire Repair Calgary — $50 Per Tire
settings.subheading: Picked up a nail on Deerfoot, or fighting a slow leak? Flat tire repair at Prince Tires is $50 per tire — a permanent internal patch warrantied for the life of the tire, done in 20-30 minutes, same-day at our SW Calgary shop.
settings.pricing_intro: Flat tire repair costs $50 per tire at Prince Tires — one flat price, no shop fee. That covers dismounting the tire, finding the puncture, sealing it from the inside with a warrantied internal patch, then remounting the wheel and resetting the TPMS, all in about 20-30 minutes. We rebalance if the wheel needs it rather than billing it by default. A plug jammed in from the outside is a temporary get-home fix, not a repair — the internal patch is the only method tire manufacturers recognize. If the puncture is in the sidewall or the tire was driven flat, we'll tell you straight — that one needs replacing.

settings.lead: You're topping up the same tire again and again
settings.text: A healthy tire loses about 1 PSI a month. If one wheel needs air every week or two, something is letting it out. In a Calgary winter this gets confusing, because cold alone drops pressure roughly 1-2 PSI for every 5°C the temperature falls. The tell is that only one tire is doing it.

settings.lead: You can see a nail or screw head in the tread
settings.text: Don't pull it out. The object is plugging its own hole, and yanking it in a parking lot turns a slow leak into a flat tire. Leave it, drive straight to the shop, and we'll take it out properly with the tire off the rim.

settings.lead: The TPMS light keeps coming back after you reset it
settings.text: A sensor that re-triggers within days isn't faulty. It's doing its job and telling you the tire is genuinely losing pressure.

settings.lead: The tire is sitting low after a pothole
settings.text: April and May are the worst of it in Calgary. A hard hit on 16th Ave, McKnight or Glenmore can crack a rim or break the bead seal, and neither of those is a puncture. Neither is a puncture, and both need the wheel itself inspected, not just the tire.

settings.lead: There's a bulge or blister in the sidewall
settings.text: This one isn't a repair. A bulge means the internal cords have failed and the tire can let go at highway speed. Bring it in, but expect to replace it.

settings.heading: How to tell if your tire needs repair
settings.intro:
Most punctures don't blow out. They leak. You top the tire up at the gas station, it's fine for a week, then the light comes back on. That slow cycle usually means a nail or screw is still sitting in the tread, sealing its own hole just well enough to hide.

Here's what tells you it's time to bring it in.
settings.outro: If you're not sure which of these you've got, bring the vehicle in. We'll put the tire in the water tank and find the leak instead of guessing.

settings.lead: We take the tire off the rim
settings.text: A proper repair can't be done with the tire mounted. This is the step that separates a real fix from a plug jammed in at the roadside.

settings.lead: We inspect it from the inside
settings.text: With the tire off, we can see the damage the way it actually is: how big the hole is, what angle it went in at, and whether the inner liner got chewed up from driving on it low. Some punctures never show from the outside at all, and this is the step that finds them.

settings.lead: We seal it with a patch-plug combination
settings.text: The plug fills the puncture channel so water and road salt can't get in and rust the belts. The patch seals the inner liner so air can't get out. Applied from the inside, as one unit. This is the method tire manufacturers recognize as a permanent repair.

settings.lead: We remount the wheel and reset your TPMS
settings.text: Including re-seating the bead and getting the sensor talking to the vehicle again, so you're not driving away with a warning light on. If the wheel needs rebalancing after the repair we'll do it. We don't add it to every ticket by default.

settings.lead: Warrantied for the life of the tire
settings.text: If a repair we did fails, bring it back. The warranty runs as long as the tire does.

settings.heading: What's included in a $50 tire repair
settings.intro: One price, per tire, no shop fee added at the counter. What that covers:
settings.outro: Appointments are served first, so booking a slot online is the fastest way through. Walk-ins are welcome and we'll fit you in around the booked work. Book a flat tire repair or call (403) 452-4283.

settings.lead: Sidewall damage
settings.text: The sidewall flexes with every rotation. A patch there won't stay bonded, and the failure happens at speed. This includes the bulges that show up after a pothole.

settings.lead: Punctures in the shoulder
settings.text: The shoulder is the curved part where the tread wraps toward the sidewall. It flexes nearly as much as the sidewall does, so the repairable zone stops before it. A nail 2 cm too far out is the difference between a $50 fix and a new tire.

settings.lead: Anything larger than a quarter inch
settings.text: About 6 mm, roughly a standard nail or screw. Past that, there isn't enough intact rubber and steel around the hole for a patch to hold.

settings.lead: A tire that's already been repaired in the same spot
settings.text: Overlapping patches don't bond reliably. Separate punctures elsewhere in the tread are usually fine.

settings.lead: A tire that was driven flat
settings.text: Running on a deflated tire destroys the inner liner, even over a short distance. The outside can look untouched while the inside has come apart. It doesn't take much distance either. An exit ramp and a few blocks is enough to do it.

settings.heading: When a tire can't be safely repaired
settings.intro: We'd rather patch your tire than sell you a new one, and most punctures are fixable. But some damage can't be repaired safely, and no honest shop will tell you otherwise. These are the ones we turn down.
settings.outro: If we can't repair it, we'll show you the damage and explain why before anything gets replaced. You can see what we stock at our tire pages, or read how Calgary potholes wreck tires.

settings.lead: Get off the road before you inspect anything
settings.text: An exit, a side street, a parking lot. Not the shoulder of Deerfoot or Stoney if you can help it.

settings.lead: Don't drive on it flat
settings.text: This is the single thing that turns a repairable puncture into a write-off. A tire that's low can often be limped a short distance at low speed. A tire that's flat cannot.

settings.lead: Leave the nail where it is
settings.text: It's slowing the leak. Pulling it out on the roadside just empties the tire faster.

settings.lead: A plug kit is an emergency measure, not a repair
settings.text: If you're stranded after hours with no other option, a plug can get you off the road. It is not a fix. It seals from the outside, leaves the inner liner open, and lets salt and water reach the steel belts. Bring it in and we'll do it properly.

settings.lead: Book the repair rather than waiting it out
settings.text: A slow leak doesn't heal. It gets worse in the cold, and driving on a chronically underinflated tire wears the shoulders and costs you fuel.

settings.heading: What to do when you get a flat in Calgary
settings.intro: Construction season on Deerfoot means nails and screws on the road, and spring means potholes. If you pick one up, what you do in the next ten minutes decides whether it's a $50 repair or a new tire.
